subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Roots and Prefixes — Meaning from Word Structure (W11 B1)

questions.stem: The root 'BENE' (as in BENEFICIAL, BENEVOLENT) means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'BENE' = good/well (Latin). Examples: Beneficial (producing good results), Benevolent (well-wishing, kind), Benefactor (one who does good deeds), Benign (kind, harmless). Antonym root: 'MAL' = bad/evil (malevolent, malicious, malefactor). Trap: 'Below' = 'sub-'; 'Against' = 'anti-' or 'contra-'; 'Bad' = 'mal-'.

questions.stem: The suffix '-CIDE' (as in HOMICIDE, PESTICIDE, PATRICIDE) means:
questions.explanation: C is correct. '-CIDE' = killing of (Latin: caedere = to kill). Homicide = killing of a human; Pesticide = killer of pests; Patricide = killing of one's father; Genocide = killing of a racial group; Infanticide = killing of an infant. Trap: 'Study of' = '-ology'; 'Rule of' = '-cracy'; 'Fear of' = '-phobia'.

questions.stem: Which word uses the root 'LOGY' (meaning 'study of') INCORRECTLY?
questions.explanation: B is incorrect. ANTHOLOGY does NOT mean 'study of flowers'. ANTHOLOGY = a collection of literary works (poems, stories). Root: 'antho' = flower + 'logia' = collection — originally a 'gathering of flowers' used metaphorically for a collection of literary pieces. The word for 'study of flowers' is BOTANY or specifically ANTHOLOGY is wrongly associated with 'study'. 'ANTHROLOGY' doesn't exist; the correct term would be part of BOTANY. Geology ✓ (geo=earth), Zoology ✓ (zoo=animal), Physiology ✓ (physio=nature/function).

questions.stem: The prefix 'PHIL' or 'PHILO' (as in PHILOSOPHY, PHILANTHROPIST) means:
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'PHIL/PHILO' = love (Greek: philos = loving/beloved). Philosophy = love of wisdom (sophia = wisdom). Philanthropist = lover of humanity (anthropos = human). Bibliophile = book lover. Antonym: 'MISO' = hatred (misanthrope = one who hates humanity). Trap: Fear = phob-; Hatred = miso-; Wisdom = sophia (component in philosophy but not the prefix).

questions.stem: Which pair correctly pairs a '-CRACY' suffix word with its meaning?

options.option_text: Theocracy — rule by the church/religious leaders
Ochlocracy — rule by a single individual

questions.explanation: B is correct. '-CRACY' = rule/government (Greek: kratos = power). THEOCRACY = rule by God or religious leaders (theos = God). Plutocracy = rule by the wealthy (ploutos = wealth). Ochlocracy = rule by the mob (ochlos = mob). Meritocracy = rule by the most able/talented (merit = deserved reward). Trap: Plutocracy ≠ military (that's stratocracy); Ochlocracy ≠ individual rule (that's autocracy/monarchy); Meritocracy ≠ elderly (that's gerontocracy).

questions.stem: The prefix 'ANTE' (as in ANTECEDENT, ANTEROOM) means:
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'ANTE' = before (Latin). Antecedent = something that comes before; Anteroom = a room before another/a waiting room. Compare with 'ANTI' (= against) — these are commonly confused. 'Ante-' = before (in time or space); 'Anti-' = against or opposed to. Other 'ante-' words: antenatal (before birth), antediluvian (before the flood = very old). Trap: Against = anti-; After = post-; Below = sub-.

questions.stem: Which word does NOT contain the root 'CHRON' (= time, from Greek 'chronos')?
questions.explanation: C is correct. ANTHOLOGY does NOT contain the 'chron' root. Anthology = a collection of literary works; root = 'antho' (Greek: flower) + 'logia' (collection) — literally a 'gathering of flowers' used metaphorically. It has nothing to do with time. The other three all use 'chron': Chronological (chrono = time + logos = order/study), Synchronize (syn = together + chron = at the same time), Anachronism (ana = against + chron = wrong in time). Trap: 'Synchronize' starts with 'sy' so students might miss the 'chron' inside it.

questions.stem: The root 'BREV' (as in BRIEF, ABBREVIATE, BREVITY) means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'BREV' = short (Latin: brevis). Brief = short; Brevity = shortness/conciseness; Abbreviate = to shorten; Breve (music) = a short note. Antonym: 'LONG/LONGI' = long (longitude, elongate). Trap: 'Long' is the exact antonym of 'brev-'; 'Wide' = 'lati-'; 'Strong' = 'fort-'.

questions.stem: Which word correctly uses the prefix 'PSEUDO' (= false, fake)?

options.option_text: Pseudonym — a real name used in publications
Pseudonym — a false or pen name used instead of one's real name
Pseudonym — an abbreviation of a long name
Pseudonym — a name given at birth

questions.explanation: B is correct. PSEUDONYM = a false or assumed name (pseudo = false, nym = name). Authors use pseudonyms to publish under a different name. Examples: George Eliot (Mary Ann Evans), Mark Twain (Samuel Clemens). Other 'pseudo-' words: Pseudoscience (false science), Pseudopod (false foot — structure in amoeba). Trap: A says 'real name' (opposite); C and D give wrong definitions.

questions.stem: The root 'GREG' (as in AGGREGATE, CONGREGATE, SEGREGATE) means:
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'GREG' = flock/herd/crowd (Latin: grex). Aggregate = gather into a mass (ad + grex); Congregate = gather together (con + grex); Segregate = separate from the flock (se + grex); Gregarious = sociable, fond of being in a group. Trap: 'To lead' = 'ag-' or 'duc-'; 'To separate' is what 'segregate' does but the root itself means 'flock'; 'To measure' = 'metr-'.
